sources.notes: Legacy pre-2007 Composite Document Format .doc; readfile.aspx's Format=HTML/PDF/TEXT variants all return an identical 60-page scanned image with no text layer, so this Word download is the only machine-readable copy the state publishes. capture.py converts it with textutil (macOS built-in, tried first by capture-core's converter list); the original 2026-08-30 hand capture used libreoffice --headless --convert-to txt instead, and the two converters format the same bytes slightly differently, so anchors here were re-derived against a fresh textutil conversion rather than reused verbatim from the standing packet. Section 4.13 (Admission, Transfer and Discharge) is a single contiguous span in the source document; this slice widens one section either side of it (4.12 and 4.14) to hold whole sections rather than cut mid-provision.

sources.title: BMS Provider Manual, Chapter 514 Nursing Facility Services — transfer/discharge policy and bed reservation
sources.notes: West Virginia's Medicaid provider manual, published by the Bureau for Medical Services, restates the transfer/discharge policy in its own words (514.8.2) and states the state's Medicaid bed-hold rule (514.8.3), which no licensure source captured as sources 1-3 states. The heading text '514.8.2 Transfer and Discharge Policies' and '514.8.4 Medical Leave of Absence' each appear twice -- once in the table of contents, once at the real heading -- so from_occurrence 2 is used to land on the body; the 'to' anchor's own occurrence count restarts after the 'from' match, so the single body occurrence of the 514.8.4 heading needs no occurrence override. This document's page break carries a six-line footer/header block (a 'BMS Provider Manual / Page NN / Chapter 514... / Effective: 10/1/2024' line pair, a three-line DISCLAIMER paragraph, and a 'CHAPTER 514 NURSING FACILITY SERVICES' banner) -- taller than strip-running-headers' two-line edge window reaches, so that filter (tried, and left off this source since it changed nothing) cannot drop it. The boilerplate survives in the packet between provisions; every quotation in this page's markdown was chosen to fall within a single printed page rather than crossing one of these breaks. See this state's change log and QUEUE.md.
